{"content": "# Hermes Agent -- Docker\n\nRun [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) by **Nous Research**\ninside a lean Debian container and connect from an external GUI client.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n  +--------------------------------------------+\n  |  Host                                      |\n  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |\n  |  | ./input/         |-->| /data/ro       | |  Read-only input\n  |  | (host dir)       |   | (container)    | |\n  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |\n  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |\n  |  | ./workspace/     |<--| /data/rw       | |  Read-write work data\n  |  | (host dir)       |   | (container)    | |\n  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |\n  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |\n  |  | ./hermes-        |-->| /config        | |  Persistent config\n  |  | config/          |   | (yaml + .env)  | |\n  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |\n  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |\n  |  | /path/to/vault   |-->| /vault         | |  Optional Obsidian vault\n  |  | (host dir)       |   | (container)    | |  (read-write, opt-in)\n  |  +------------------+   +----------------+ |\n  |                                            |\n  |  GUI client --port 8080--> container      |\n  +--------------------------------------------+\n```\n\n## Files\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|------|---------|\n| `Dockerfile` | Multi-stage build (bookworm-slim) |\n| `docker-compose.yml` | Service definition + init service |\n| `docker-entrypoint.sh` | Config check, initialisation, server start |\n| `.env.example` | Environment variable template (copy to `.env`) |\n| `README.md` | This document |\n\n## Build\n\n```bash\ndocker compose build\n```\n\nTo pin a specific Hermes version, set `HERMES_COMMIT` in `.env` or pass it\nas a build arg:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose build --build-arg HERMES_COMMIT=abc123def\n```\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### 1. Provide Configuration\n\n**Option A -- Pre-made config (recommended for automation):**\n\nCreate two files inside `./hermes-config/`:\n\n**`hermes-config/config.yaml`**:\n```yaml\nserver:\n  host: 0.0.0.0\n  port: 8080\n```\n\n**`hermes-config/.env`**:\n```bash\n# At least one LLM provider API key\nOPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...\n```\n\n**Option B -- Interactive setup (run once):**\n\n```bash\ndocker compose run --rm hermes-init\n```\n\nThe wizard steps you through provider, model, and API key choices. The\ngenerated config is saved to `./hermes-config/` and is picked up by the\nregular service afterwards.\n\n### 2. Start\n\n```bash\ndocker compose up -d\n```\n\n### 3. Connect\n\nPoint your Hermes GUI client (desktop app) at:\n\n```\nhttp://<host-ip>:8080\n```\n\n## Port Configuration\n\n```bash\n# Via .env\nHERMES_PORT=9090\n\n# Or inline\nHERMES_PORT=9090 docker compose up -d\n```\n\n## Data Directories\n\n| Host path | Container | Mode | Purpose |\n|-----------|-----------|------|---------|\n| `./input/` | `/data/ro` | `:ro` | Read-only host input data |\n| `./workspace/` | `/data/rw` | `:rw` | Read-write work and results |\n| `./hermes-config/` | `/config` | `:rw` | Persistent configuration + secrets |\n| *(optional)* `/vault` | `/vault` | `:rw` | Optional Obsidian vault mount |\n\n## Optional Obsidian Vault Mount\n\nYou can optionally mount an existing Obsidian vault into the container so\nHermes has read/write access to it -- the same freedom it has with its own\nHermes Vault (HV) in a non-Docker setup.\n\nThis is **purely optional**. The container works perfectly without it.\n\n### How It Works\n\n- The vault is mounted at `/vault` inside the container.\n- Hermes runs as the `hermes` user and has full r/w access to everything\n  under `/vault`.\n- The standard Hermes tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `search_files`,\n  `patch`) work on `/vault/...` paths without extra configuration.\n- Hermes can browse, create, and edit notes, search file contents, and\n  manage markdown files -- everything it does with its own HV.\n\n### Setup\n\nUncomment and adjust the vault volume in `docker-compose.yml`:\n\n```yaml\nvolumes:\n  # ... other mounts ...\n  - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw\n```\n\nReplace the path with your actual vault location, for example:\n\n```yaml\n  - /home/user/syncthing/obsidian-vault:/vault:rw\n```\n\n### UID/GID Considerations\n\nThe container user `hermes` has UID 1000 by default (configurable via build\nargs `USER_ID`/`GROUP_ID`). Your vault files must be readable and writable\nby that UID. The two easiest approaches:\n\n1. **Match the build UID to your host user** (recommended):\n   ```bash\n   docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)\n   ```\n\n2. **Make vault files group-accessible**:\n   ```bash\n   chmod -R g+rws /path/to/your/vault\n   ```\n\n### What Hermes Can Do With the Vault\n\nOnce mounted, Hermes can perform all vault operations it normally does with\nits own HV:\n\n| Operation | How |\n|-----------|-----|\n| Read notes | `read_file(path=\"/vault/some-note.md\")` |\n| Write new notes | `write_file(path=\"/vault/new-note.md\", content=\"...\")` |\n| Search contents | `search_files(pattern=\"...\", path=\"/vault\")` |\n| Patch existing notes | `patch(path=\"/vault/some-note.md\", old_string=\"...\", new_string=\"...\")` |\n| Navigate directories | `terminal(command=\"ls /vault/\")` |\n| Create/manage markdown | All standard Hermes tools |\n\nThe entrypoint script detects the vault mount on startup and reports\nwhether an Obsidian vault (`.obsidian/` marker) is present.\n\n## Permission Model (UID/GID)\n\nThe Hermes process runs as user `hermes` (UID 1000 / GID 1000 by default).\n\n**If your host user has a different UID:**\n\n1. Check your UID:\n   ```bash\n   id -u\n   ```\n\n2. Rebuild with matching UID:\n   ```bash\n   docker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)\n   ```\n\n3. Ensure `./workspace/` is writable on the host:\n   ```bash\n   mkdir -p workspace input hermes-config\n   chmod 755 workspace\n   ```\n\n4. Or fix permissions after the first start:\n   ```bash\n   chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) workspace\n   ```\n\n## Initialisation Strategy\n\n### The Problem\n\n`hermes setup` is an interactive wizard. In a headless container it must\nnot block unattended.\n\n### The Solution\n\nThe entrypoint script (`docker-entrypoint.sh`) checks on startup:\n\n1. **Does `/config/config.yaml` exist?**\n   - **Yes** -- Start the server directly.\n   - **No** -- Create a minimal config. The container starts, but without an\n     LLM provider configured. API keys must be provided separately via\n     `/config/.env` (Option A above).\n\n2. **Does `/config/.env` exist?**\n   - **No** -- Warning with instructions to add API keys.\n   - **Yes** -- No action.\n\n3. **Fallback (neither config nor .env):**\n   The container exits with a clear error message and non-zero exit code.\n   No stuck wizard.\n\n### Container Commands\n\n| Command | Effect |\n|---------|--------|\n| `docker compose up -d` | Normal server operation |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` | Interactive setup wizard (one-time) |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes config get default.model` | Read config values |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes shell` | Debug shell inside container |\n\n## Health Check\n\nA TCP connect check polls whether the Hermes server is listening on the\nconfigured port:\n\n```yaml\nhealthcheck:\n  test: [\"CMD\", \"bash\", \"-c\", \"exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT} 2>/dev/null\"]\n  interval: 30s\n  timeout: 10s\n  retries: 3\n  start_period: 30s\n```\n\nNote: Hermes serve has no dedicated HTTP health endpoint. The TCP check is\na best-effort liveness signal -- a positive check means the port is open,\nnot necessarily that Hermes is fully initialised.\n\n## Security\n\nThe container runs with restricted privileges:\n\n- **Non-root user:** `hermes` (UID/GID 1000, configurable at build time)\n- **No new privileges:** `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true`\n- **No unnecessary capabilities:** `cap_drop: [ALL]`\n- **Write access only to:** `/config`, `/data/rw`, and optionally `/vault`\n  (all mounted as volumes)\n\n## Logging\n\n```bash\ndocker compose logs -f\n```\n\nHermes writes no persistent log files in serve mode (output goes to\nstdout/stderr). For detailed diagnostics:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose run --rm hermes doctor\n```\n\n## Backup\n\nThe only data that cannot be regenerated is the configuration:\n\n```bash\ntar czf hermes-config-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz hermes-config/\n```\n\nRestore:\n\n```bash\ntar xzf hermes-config-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz\n```\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---------|-------|-----|\n| Container exits immediately | Config missing | Create `./hermes-config/config.yaml` or run `hermes-init` |\n| `hermes: command not found` | Build failure | `docker compose build --no-cache` |\n| Cannot connect to server | Port not exposed | Check `docker compose ps`, fix port in `.env` |\n| Permission denied on `/data/rw` | UID mismatch | Adjust build UID (see Permission Model) |\n| \"No API key configured\" | `.env` missing or empty | Add API key to `./hermes-config/.env` |\n| Vault not writable from inside | UID mismatch on vault files | Match `USER_ID` build arg to vault owner's UID |\n\n## Known Limitations\n\n- **No desktop app build inside container:** The desktop app (Electron) is\n  not built inside the container. The `serve` command provides the\n  JSON-RPC/WebSocket backend that desktop, TUI, or web clients connect to\n  from outside.\n- **Health check is TCP-only:** Hermes serve has no HTTP health endpoint.\n- **`--insecure` is DEPRECATED:** Since the June 2026 hardening, binding on\n  a public interface always requires an auth provider regardless of this\n  flag. Use a tunnel (SSH/WireGuard) to 127.0.0.1 for local-only access.", "path": "/daten/home/rb/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker/README.md"}

{"success": true, "name": "hermes-agent", "file": "references/providers-and-models.md", "content": "# Providers & Model Aliases\n\nSet via `hermes model` (picker) or `hermes setup`. 35+ provider profiles ship as\nplugins under `plugins/model-providers/`; user plugins of the same name override.\nFull docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers\n\n### Providers\n\n| Provider | Auth | Key env var(s) |\n|----------|------|----------------|\n| openrouter | API key | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |\n| anthropic | API key | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (also `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) |\n| nous | OAuth device code | `hermes auth add nous` (or `NOUS_API_KEY`) |\n| openai-codex | OAuth | `hermes auth add openai-codex` |\n| qwen-oauth | OAuth | `hermes auth add qwen-oauth` |\n| minimax-oauth | OAuth | `hermes auth add minimax-oauth` |\n| copilot | Token | `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` (Copilot device flow — `gh auth login` tokens do NOT work) |\n| copilot-acp | External CLI | Copilot CLI on PATH or `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` |\n| gemini | API key | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` |\n| xai | API key | `XAI_API_KEY` (SuperGrok OAuth also supported) |\n| deepseek | API key | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |\n| zai (GLM) | API key | `GLM_API_KEY` / `ZAI_API_KEY` |\n| minimax / minimax-cn | API key | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` / `MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY` |\n| kimi-coding / -cn | API key | `KIMI_API_KEY` / `KIMI_CN_API_KEY` |\n| alibaba (+coding-plan) | API key | `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY` / `ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY` |\n| xiaomi | API key | `XIAOMI_API_KEY` |\n| huggingface | Token | `HF_TOKEN` |\n| fireworks / novita / nvidia / deepinfra / gmi / arcee / stepfun / upstage / kilocode / ai-gateway / opencode-zen / opencode-go / ollama-cloud | API key | `<NAME>_API_KEY` |\n| bedrock / vertex / azure-foundry | Cloud SDK / key | AWS SDK creds / Vertex ADC / `AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY` |\n| custom | Config | `model.base_url` + `model.api_key` in config.yaml |\n\nMultiple credentials per provider pool and rotate automatically (`hermes auth`).\nFallback chain when the primary fails: `hermes fallback add|remove|list`.\n\n### User-defined model aliases\n\nWork with `/model <name>` in CLI and every gateway platform. Resolved by\n`hermes_cli/model_switch.py::resolve_alias()`; user aliases are checked BEFORE\nthe built-in table, so a user `sonnet`/`grok` shadows the built-in.\n\n```yaml\n# Full form\nmodel_aliases:\n  fav:\n    model: claude-sonnet-4.6\n    provider: anthropic\n  local-qwen:\n    model: qwen3.5:397b\n    provider: custom\n    base_url: \"https://ollama.com/v1\"\n  theta:\n    model: theta-1\n    provider: custom\n    base_url: \"https://theta.example.com/v1\"\n    key_env: THETA_API_KEY        # or: api_key: \"${THETA_API_KEY}\"\n\n# Short form (\"provider/model\"), also via CLI:\n#   hermes config set model.aliases.fav openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6\nmodel:\n  aliases:\n    fav: openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6\n```\n\n`/model fav` — session-scoped; add `--global` to persist as default.\n\nAn alias with its own `base_url` authenticates with its own credential\n(`api_key`, which also accepts a `\"${VAR}\"` reference, or `key_env`). With\nneither set the key is resolved from the alias HOST, never carried over from\nthe provider that was active before the switch.\n\nBuilt-in aliases (catalog-resolved against the active provider): `sonnet`,\n`opus`, `haiku`, `claude`, `gpt5`, `gpt`, `codex`, `o3`, `o4`, `gemini`,\n`deepseek`, `grok`, `llama`, `qwen`, `minimax`, `nemotron`, `kimi`, `glm`,\n`step`, `mimo`, `trinity`.\n", "file_type": ".md", "_source_path": "/home/rb/.hermes/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/hermes-agent/references/providers-and-models.md"}

Your vault files must be readable and writable\n157|by that UID. Check your UID:\n193|   ```bash\n194|   id -u\n195|   ```\n196|\n197|2. In a headless container it must\n218|not block unattended.\n219|\n220|### The Solution\n221|\n222|The entrypoint script (`docker-entrypoint.sh`) checks on startup:\n223|\n224|1. **Does `/config/config.yaml` exist?**\n225|   - **Yes** -- Start the server directly.\n226|   - **No** -- Create a minimal config. The container starts, but without an\n227|     LLM provider configured. API keys must be provided separately via\n228|     `/config/.env` (Option A above).\n229|\n230|2. **Does `/config/.env` exist?**\n231|   - **No** -- Warning with instructions to add API keys.\n232|   - **Yes** -- No action.\n233|\n234|3. **Fallback (neither config nor .env):**\n235|   The container exits with a clear error message and non-zero exit code.\n236|   No stuck wizard.\n237|\n238|### Container Commands\n239|\n240|| Command | Effect |\n241||---------|--------|\n242|| `docker compose up -d` | Normal server operation |\n243|| `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` | Interactive setup wizard (one-time) |\n244|| `docker compose run --rm hermes config get default.model` | Read config values |\n245|| `docker compose run --rm hermes shell` | Debug shell inside container |\n246|\n247|## Health Check\n248|\n249|A TCP connect check polls whether the Hermes server is listening on the\n250|configured port:\n251|\n252|```yaml\n253|healthcheck:\n254|  test: [\"CMD\", \"bash\", \"-c\", \"exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT} 2>/dev/null\"]\n255|  interval: 30s\n256|  timeout: 10s\n257|  retries: 3\n258|  start_period: 30s\n259|```\n260|\n261|Note: Hermes serve has no dedicated HTTP health endpoint. The TCP check is\n262|a best-effort liveness signal -- a positive check means the port is open,\n263|not necessarily that Hermes is fully initialised.\n264|\n265|## Security\n266|\n267|The container runs with restricted privileges:\n268|\n269|- **Non-root user:** `hermes` (UID/GID 1000, configurable at build time)\n270|- **No new privileges:** `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true`\n271|- **No unnecessary capabilities:** `cap_drop: [ALL]`\n272|- **Write access only to:** `/config`, `/data/rw`, and optionally `/vault`\n273|  (all mounted as volumes)\n274|\n275|## Logging\n276|\n277|```bash\n278|docker compose logs -f\n279|```\n280|\n281|Hermes writes no persistent log files in serve mode (output goes to\n282|stdout/stderr). On Linux with a desktop environment, the cleanest approaches are: 1. **systemd --user service**: Starts when the user logs in (via PAM or display manager), stops when the user logs out. Best for terminal/server use. 2. **Desktop autostart (.desktop file)**: For GUI desktop environments (KDE, GNOME, etc.) 3. **bash .bash_profile / .bash_logout**: Simplest, but fragile and only works in terminal sessions. Systemd --user is the most robust. {"content": "# Hermes Agent -- Docker\n\nRun [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) by **Nous Research**\ninside a lean Debian container and connect from an external GUI client.\n\n## Project Files\n\n```\nhermes-inside-docker/\n|-- Dockerfile                    Multi-stage build (bookworm-slim)\n|-- docker-compose.yml            Service + init service definition\n|-- docker-entrypoint.sh          Config check, initialisation, server start\n|-- hermes-launcher.sh            Wrapper that finds the venv Python at runtime\n|-- hermes-docker.service         systemd --user autostart (login = start, logout = stop)\n|-- generate-password-hash.sh     Helper: generate a bcrypt password hash\n|-- .env.example                  Environment variable template (copy to .env)\n|-- README.md                     This document\n|-- examples/\n|   |-- config.openai.yaml        Config for OpenAI\n|   |-- config.openrouter.yaml    Config for OpenRouter\n|   +-- config.custom-openai.yaml Config for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint\n```\n\n## Quick Start (5 minutes)\n\n### 1. Build the Image\n\n```bash\ncd hermes-inside-docker\ndocker compose build\n```\n\nThis takes 3-5 minutes on first run (downloads Debian packages, clones Hermes,\ninstalls Python dependencies, builds the web UI). Subsequent builds are cached.\n\n### 2. Configure\n\nChoose a provider and copy the matching example config:\n\n```bash\n# Option A: OpenAI\ncp examples/config.openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml\n\n# Option B: OpenRouter\ncp examples/config.openrouter.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml\n\n# Option C: Custom OpenAI-compatible (corporate API, self-hosted vLLM, etc.)\ncp examples/config.custom-openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml\n\n# Option D: Interactive wizard (one-time)\n# docker compose run --rm hermes-init\n```\n\n### 3. Set API Keys\n\nCreate `hermes-config/.env` with your API key:\n\n```bash\n# OpenAI\necho \"OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...\" > hermes-config/.env\n\n# Or OpenRouter\necho \"OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...\" > hermes-config/.env\n\n# Or custom provider\necho \"CUSTOM_API_KEY=sk-...\" > hermes-config/.env\n```\n\n### 4. (Important) Set a Password\n\nThe Hermes server binds to `0.0.0.0` (all network interfaces). Since the\nJune 2026 hardening, this requires an auth provider. The example configs\ninclude a demo password (`admin` / `demo`). **Change it immediately:**\n\n```bash\n# Generate a hash for your own password:\n./generate-password-hash.sh your-secure-password\n```\n\nCopy the output into `hermes-config/config.yaml` under `dashboard.basic_auth`.\n\n### 5. Start the Server\n\n```bash\ndocker compose up -d\n```\n\n### 6. Connect\n\nPoint your Hermes GUI client (desktop app, web dashboard, or any JSON-RPC\ncompatible client) at:\n\n```\nhttp://<host-ip>:8080\n```\n\nYour browser will ask for the username and password configured in step 4.\n\n---\n\n## Detailed Guide\n\n### Provider Configuration\n\nAll example configs are in `examples/`. Each sets the model provider and\nincludes a password auth block. Pick one:\n\n| File | Provider | API Key Env Var |\n|------|----------|-----------------|\n| `config.openai.yaml` | OpenAI (`openai`) | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |\n| `config.openrouter.yaml` | OpenRouter (`openrouter`) | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |\n| `config.custom-openai.yaml` | Custom (`custom` + `base_url`) | `CUSTOM_API_KEY` |\n\n**Custom provider (e.g. corporate API gateway):**\n\nEdit `examples/config.custom-openai.yaml` and set the `base_url` to your\nprovider's endpoint:\n\n```yaml\nmodel:\n  default: gpt-4o-mini\n  provider: custom\n  base_url: \"https://api.your-company.com/v1\"\n  api_key: \"${CUSTOM_API_KEY}\"\n```\n\n### Auth: Three Ways to Handle 0.0.0.0 Binding\n\nThe Hermes server refuses to bind to `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces) without\nauthentication. Choose one:\n\n#### A) Password Auth (recommended)\n\nAlready included in all example configs. Generate your own hash:\n\n```bash\n./generate-password-hash.sh my-password\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\ndashboard:\n  basic_auth:\n    username: admin\n    password_hash: \"scrypt$16384$8$1$...\"\n```\n\nPaste this block into `hermes-config/config.yaml`.\n\n#### B) SSH Tunnel (no auth)\n\nBind to `127.0.0.1` in config.yaml:\n\n```yaml\nserver:\n  host: 127.0.0.1\n  port: 8080\n```\n\nTunnel from your client machine:\n\n```bash\nssh -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 user@docker-host\n```\n\nThen connect to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` on your client.\n\n#### C) WireGuard Tunnel (no auth)\n\nSame principle: bind to `127.0.0.1`, forward the port through WireGuard.\n\n### Data Directories\n\n| Host Path | Container Path | Mode | Purpose |\n|-----------|---------------|------|---------|\n| `./input/` | `/data/ro` | `:ro` | Read-only input data from host |\n| `./workspace/` | `/data/rw` | `:rw` | Read-write work and results |\n| `./hermes-config/` | `/config` | `:rw` | Persistent config (yaml + .env) |\n| *(optional)* | `/vault` | `:rw` | Obsidian vault (opt-in, see below) |\n\n### Optional Obsidian Vault Mount\n\nMount an existing Obsidian vault so Hermes can read, write, search, and\npatch notes -- the same full access it has with its own HV.\n\nUncomment the vault volume in `docker-compose.yml`:\n\n```yaml\nvolumes:\n  - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw\n```\n\nHermes detects the mount on startup and logs whether it contains an\n`.obsidian/` marker. All Hermes tools (`read_file`, `write_file`,\n`search_files`, `patch`) work on `/vault/...` paths without extra config.\n\n### Permission Model (UID/GID)\n\nThe container user `hermes` has UID 1000 / GID 1000 by default. If your\nhost user has a different UID, rebuild:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)\n```\n\n### Container Commands\n\n| Command | Effect |\n|---------|--------|\n| `docker compose up -d` | Start server in background |\n| `docker compose down` | Stop server |\n| `docker compose logs -f` | Follow log output |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` | Interactive setup wizard (one-time) |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes config get default.model` | Read a config value |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes shell` | Debug shell inside container |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes doctor` | Hermes diagnostics |\n\n---\n\n## Autostart: Start on Login, Stop on Logout\n\nThe project includes a **systemd --user service** that:\n- **Starts** the Hermes container when you log in\n- **Stops** it when you log out\n- **Restarts** it automatically if it crashes\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- `systemd --user` must be available (default on most Linux distributions\n  with GNOME, KDE, or similar desktop environments)\n- Docker must be installed and running\n\n### Installation\n\n```bash\n# 1. Copy the service file to your user systemd directory\nmkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user/\ncp hermes-docker.service ~/.config/systemd/user/\n\n# 2. Edit the path in the service file to match your project location\nnano ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service\n# Change \"WorkingDirectory=%h/...\" to the actual absolute path of your\n# hermes-inside-docker directory, for example:\n#   WorkingDirectory=/home/rb/hermes-inside-docker\n#\n# %h expands to your home directory at runtime. Use the full path if\n# your project is outside your home.\n\n# 3. Reload systemd, enable, and start\nsystemctl --user daemon-reload\nsystemctl --user enable hermes-docker\nsystemctl --user start hermes-docker\n```\n\n### Verification\n\n```bash\n# Check if it's running\nsystemctl --user status hermes-docker\n\n# Watch logs\njournalctl --user -u hermes-docker -f\n\n# Test the lifecycle: log out and back in, then check\nsystemctl --user status hermes-docker\n# Should show \"active (exited)\" after login\n```\n\n### How It Works\n\n- `WantedBy=default.target` tells systemd to start this service whenever\n  the user session starts (i.e., on login).\n- `Type=oneshot` + `RemainAfterExit=yes` means the service runs the start\n  command, records itself as active, and runs the stop command when stopped.\n- When the user logs out, systemd --user terminates, which stops all user\n  services including this one.\n- `Restart=on-failure` ensures the container restarts if Docker restarts\n  or the container crashes.\n\n### Uninstall\n\n```bash\nsystemctl --user stop hermes-docker\nsystemctl --user disable hermes-docker\nrm ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service\nsystemctl --user daemon-reload\n```\n\n### Alternative: Desktop Autostart (no systemd)\n\nIf your system doesn't use systemd --user, create a desktop autostart entry:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p ~/.config/autostart/\ncat > ~/.config/autostart/hermes-docker.desktop << 'EOF'\n[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=Hermes Agent Docker\nComment=Start Hermes container on login\nExec=docker compose -f /path/to/hermes-inside-docker/docker-compose.yml up -d\nTerminal=false\nX-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true\nEOF\n```\n\nAnd a logout script to stop it:\n\n```bash\ncat > ~/.config/autostart/hermes-docker-stop.desktop << 'EOF'\n[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=Hermes Agent Stop\nComment=Stop Hermes container on logout\nExec=docker compose -f /path/to/hermes-inside-docker/docker-compose.yml down\nTerminal=false\nX-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true\nEOF\n```\n\n---\n\n## Security\n\n- **Non-root user:** `hermes` (UID/GID 1000, configurable at build time)\n- **No new privileges:** `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true` in compose\n- **No unnecessary capabilities:** `cap_drop: [ALL]`\n- **Write access only to:** `/config`, `/data/rw`, and optionally `/vault`\n  (all mounted volumes)\n- **Auth required for public bind:** Password or OAuth since June 2026 hardening\n\n## Health Check\n\n```yaml\nhealthcheck:\n  test: [\"CMD\", \"bash\", \"-c\", \"exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT} 2>/dev/null\"]\n  interval: 30s\n  timeout: 10s\n  retries: 3\n  start_period: 30s\n```\n\nThis is a TCP connect check (Hermes serve has no HTTP health endpoint).\n\n## Backup\n\n```bash\ntar czf hermes-config-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz hermes-config/\n```\n\nRestore:\n\n```bash\ntar xzf hermes-config-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz\n```\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---------|-------|-----|\n| Container exits immediately | Config missing | Create `./hermes-config/config.yaml` or run `hermes-init` |\n| `hermes: command not found` | Build failure | `docker compose build --no-cache` |\n| Cannot connect to server | Port not exposed | Check `docker compose ps`, fix port in `.env` |\n| Permission denied on `/data/rw` | UID mismatch | Rebuild with `USER_ID=$(id -u)` |\n| \"No API key configured\" | `.env` missing or empty | Add API key to `./hermes-config/.env` |\n| Vault not writable | UID mismatch on vault files | Match `USER_ID` build arg to vault owner |\n| Server refuses to bind 0.0.0.0 | Auth not configured | Add `dashboard.basic_auth` to config.yaml (see Auth section) |\n| systemd service won't start | Path wrong in service file | Edit `WorkingDirectory` in `~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service` |\n\n## Known Limitations\n\n- **No desktop app build:** The Electron desktop app is not built inside\n  the container. `hermes serve` provides the JSON-RPC/WebSocket backend.\n- **Health check is TCP-only:** No HTTP health endpoint.\n- **Large image:** ~4.2 GB (includes Hermes' bundled tools: ffmpeg, node,\n  Python, browser agent, etc.). This is normal for a Hermes installation.\n- **Memory:** Expect ~200-400 MB RAM usage when idle.", "path": "/daten/home/rb/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker/README.md"}

{"content": "# Hermes Agent -- Docker\n\nRun [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com) by **Nous Research**\ninside a Debian container and connect from an external GUI client.\n\n## Project Files\n\n```\nhermes-inside-docker/\n  Dockerfile                    Multi-stage build (bookworm-slim)\n  docker-compose.yml            Service + init service definition\n  docker-entrypoint.sh          Config check, initialisation, server start\n  hermes-launcher.sh            Wrapper that finds the venv Python at runtime\n  hermes-docker.service         systemd --user autostart (login=start, logout=stop)\n  generate-password-hash.sh     Helper: generate an scrypt password hash\n  .env.example                  Environment variable template\n  README.md                     This document\n  examples/\n    config.openai.yaml          Config + password auth for OpenAI\n    config.openrouter.yaml      Config + password auth for OpenRouter\n    config.custom-openai.yaml   Config + password auth for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint\n```\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n  Host\n   +-------+    /data/ro (ro)        Read-only input data\n   | input |----> container\n   +-------+    /data/rw (rw)        Read-write work and results\n   |workspc|----> container\n   +-------+    /config (rw)         Persistent config (yaml + .env)\n   |config |----> container\n   +-------+    /vault (rw)          Optional Obsidian vault (opt-in)\n   | vault |----> container\n   +-------+\n        GUI client --port 8080--> container\n```\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start -- 5 Minutes\n\n### 1. Build\n\n```bash\ncd hermes-inside-docker\ndocker compose build\n```\n\nTakes 3-5 min on first run. Subsequent builds are instant (cached).\n\n### 2. Configure\n\nPick your LLM provider and copy the matching config:\n\n```bash\n# OpenAI\ncp examples/config.openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml\n\n# OpenRouter\ncp examples/config.openrouter.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml\n\n# Corporate / self-hosted OpenAI-compatible API\ncp examples/config.custom-openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml\n```\n\n### 3. Set API Key\n\n```bash\n# OpenAI\necho \"OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...\" > hermes-config/.env\n\n# OpenRouter\necho \"OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...\" > hermes-config/.env\n\n# Custom\necho \"CUSTOM_API_KEY=sk-...\" > hermes-config/.env\n```\n\n### 4. Change Default Password (Important)\n\nThe example configs include a demo password: **username `admin`, password `demo`**.\nGenerate your own:\n\n```bash\n./generate-password-hash.sh your-secure-password\n```\n\nReplace the `password_hash` value in `hermes-config/config.yaml` with the output.\n\n### 5. Start\n\n```bash\ndocker compose up -d\n```\n\n### 6. Connect\n\nPoint your Hermes GUI client to:\n\n```\nhttp://<host-ip>:8080\n```\n\nEnter the username and password from step 4.\n\n---\n\n## Provider Configuration\n\n### OpenAI\n\n```yaml\nmodel:\n  default: gpt-4o\n  provider: openai\n```\n| Env var: `OPENAI_API_KEY`\n\n### OpenRouter\n\n```yaml\nmodel:\n  default: openai/gpt-4o\n  provider: openrouter\n```\n| Env var: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`\n\nOther models: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`, `deepseek/deepseek-chat`,\n`google/gemini-2.5-pro`.\n\n### Custom OpenAI-Compatible\n\n```yaml\nmodel:\n  default: gpt-4o-mini\n  provider: custom\n  base_url: \"https://api.your-company.com/v1\"\n  api_key: \"${CUSTOM_API_KEY}\"\n```\n| Env var: `CUSTOM_API_KEY`\n\nWorks with corporate API gateways, self-hosted vLLM/TGI, or local proxies.\n\n### Interactive Setup (Alternative)\n\n```bash\ndocker compose run --rm hermes-init\n```\n\nRuns the Hermes setup wizard interactively. Generated config is saved to\n`./hermes-config/`.\n\n---\n\n## Auth -- Required for 0.0.0.0 Binding\n\nSince June 2026, Hermes refuses to bind `serve` to `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces)\nwithout an auth provider. You have three options:\n\n| Option | Auth needed | External access |\n|--------|-------------|-----------------|\n| A. Password auth | yes | direct |\n| B. SSH tunnel | no | via tunnel |\n| C. WireGuard tunnel | no | via tunnel |\n\n### A) Password Auth (Recommended)\n\nAll example configs include a `dashboard.basic_auth` block. Generate your own:\n\n```bash\n./generate-password-hash.sh my-password\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\ndashboard:\n  basic_auth:\n    username: admin\n    password_hash: \"scrypt$16384$8$1$...\"\n```\n\nPaste into `hermes-config/config.yaml`.\n\n### B) SSH Tunnel (No Auth)\n\n```yaml\nserver:\n  host: 127.0.0.1\n  port: 8080\n```\n\n```bash\nssh -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 user@docker-host\n# Then connect to http://127.0.0.1:8080 from client machine\n```\n\n### C) WireGuard Tunnel (No Auth)\n\nSame as SSH: bind to `127.0.0.1`, forward via WireGuard.\n\n---\n\n## Port\n\n```bash\n# Via .env\nHERMES_PORT=9090\n\n# Inline\nHERMES_PORT=9090 docker compose up -d\n```\n\nDefault: 8080.\n\n---\n\n## Data Directories\n\n| Host path | Container | Mode | Purpose |\n|-----------|-----------|------|---------|\n| `./input/` | `/data/ro` | `:ro` | Read-only input from host |\n| `./workspace/` | `/data/rw` | `:rw` | Read-write work and results |\n| `./hermes-config/` | `/config` | `:rw` | Persistent configuration + API keys |\n| *(optional)* `/vault` | `/vault` | `:rw` | Obsidian vault (opt-in below) |\n\n---\n\n## Optional Obsidian Vault Mount\n\nMount an existing Obsidian vault so Hermes can read, write, search, and\npatch notes -- same full access as with its own HV.\n\n### Setup\n\nUncomment the vault volume in `docker-compose.yml`:\n\n```yaml\nvolumes:\n  - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw\n```\n\n### UID/GID Match\n\nThe container user `hermes` has UID 1000 by default. Match it to your\nhost user:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)\n```\n\n### What Works\n\n| Operation | How |\n|-----------|-----|\n| Read notes | `read_file(path=\"/vault/note.md\")` |\n| Write notes | `write_file(path=\"/vault/note.md\", content=\"...\")` |\n| Search | `search_files(pattern=\"...\", path=\"/vault\")` |\n| Patch notes | `patch(path=\"/vault/note.md\", old_string=\"...\", new_string=\"...\")` |\n| Navigate | `terminal(command=\"ls /vault/\")` |\n\nThe entrypoint detects the mount and logs whether `.obsidian/` is present.\n\n---\n\n## Permission Model\n\n```bash\n# Match UID to your host user\ndocker compose build --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g)\n```\n\nThe container runs as user `hermes` (UID/GID 1000 by default). Rebuild with\nyour UID for access to vault and workspace files.\n\n---\n\n## Container Commands\n\n| Command | Effect |\n|---------|--------|\n| `docker compose up -d` | Start server in background |\n| `docker compose down` | Stop server |\n| `docker compose logs -f` | Follow logs |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes-init` | One-time interactive setup |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes config get default.model` | Read a config value |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes shell` | Debug shell |\n| `docker compose run --rm hermes doctor` | Hermes diagnostics |\n\n---\n\n## Init Strategy -- No Stuck Wizards\n\nThe entrypoint checks on startup:\n\n1. **config.yaml exists?** Yes -> start. No -> create minimal config.\n2. **.env exists?** No -> warning with instructions.\n3. **Neither exists?** Exit with error. Never stuck in a headless wizard.\n\n---\n\n## Autostart -- Start on Login, Stop on Logout\n\nThe project includes a **systemd --user service** that starts the container\nwhen you log in and stops it when you log out.\n\n### Install\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user/\ncp hermes-docker.service ~/.config/systemd/user/\n\n# Edit the path to match your project location\nnano ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service\n# Change WorkingDirectory to the full absolute path of your\n# hermes-inside-docker directory, for example:\n#   WorkingDirectory=/home/rb/hermes-inside-docker\n\nsystemctl --user daemon-reload\nsystemctl --user enable hermes-docker\nsystemctl --user start hermes-docker\n```\n\n### Verify\n\n```bash\nsystemctl --user status hermes-docker\njournalctl --user -u hermes-docker -f\n```\n\n### How It Works\n\n- `WantedBy=default.target` -> starts when **your user session starts** (login)\n- `Type=oneshot` + `RemainAfterExit=yes` -> runs `up -d`, marks as active\n- systemd --user termination (logout) -> runs `ExecStop` -> `docker compose down`\n- `Restart=on-failure` -> auto-restart on crash or Docker daemon restart\n\n### Uninstall\n\n```bash\nsystemctl --user stop hermes-docker\nsystemctl --user disable hermes-docker\nrm ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service\nsystemctl --user daemon-reload\n```\n\n### No systemd? Desktop Autostart\n\nIf your system doesn't use systemd --user, use `.desktop` files:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p ~/.config/autostart/\n\n# Start on login\ncat > ~/.config/autostart/hermes-docker.desktop << 'EOF'\n[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=Hermes Agent\nExec=docker compose -f /home/rb/hermes-inside-docker/docker-compose.yml up -d\nTerminal=false\nX-GNOME-Autostart-enabled=true\nEOF\n\n# Stop on logout -- create a logout script in your DE settings\n```\n\n---\n\n## Security\n\n- **Non-root user:** `hermes` (UID/GID 1000, configurable)\n- **No new privileges:** `security_opt: no-new-privileges:true`\n- **No capabilities:** `cap_drop: [ALL]`\n- **Auth required for public bind:** Password or OAuth\n\n## Health Check\n\n```yaml\nhealthcheck:\n  test: [\"CMD\", \"bash\", \"-c\", \"exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/${HERMES_PORT} 2>/dev/null\"]\n  interval: 30s\n  timeout: 10s\n  retries: 3\n  start_period: 30s\n```\n\nTCP connect check (Hermes serve has no HTTP health endpoint).\n\n## Logging\n\n```bash\ndocker compose logs -f\ndocker compose run --rm hermes doctor\n```\n\n## Backup\n\n```bash\ntar czf hermes-config-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz hermes-config/\ntar xzf hermes-config-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz\n```\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n|---------|-------|-----|\n| Container exits immediately | Config missing | Create `./hermes-config/config.yaml` |\n| Cannot connect | Port not exposed | Check `docker compose ps` |\n| Permission denied | UID mismatch | Rebuild with `USER_ID=$(id -u)` |\n| \"No API key\" | `.env` missing | Add API key to `./hermes-config/.env` |\n| Refuses bind 0.0.0.0 | Auth required | Add `dashboard.basic_auth` (see Auth section) |\n| systemd service won't start | Wrong WorkingDirectory | Fix path in service file |\n\n## Known Limitations\n\n- **No desktop app build** inside container. `serve` provides JSON-RPC/WS.\n- **Health check is TCP-only.** No HTTP health endpoint.\n- **Large image** (~4.2 GB). Normal for Hermes -- includes ffmpeg, node,\n  Python, browser agent, etc.\n- **Memory:** ~200-400 MB RAM when idle.\n- **`--insecure` is DEPRECATED** since June 2026 hardening. Copy Hermes from build stage\n75|# ------------------------------------------------------------\n76|# Copy the full Hermes installation (repo, venv, tools, and the 'hermes' launcher).\n77|COPY --from=build /opt/hermes-agent /opt/hermes-agent\n78|\n79|# The 'hermes' launcher was copied into /opt/hermes-agent/bin/ during build.\n80|# It hardcodes the hermetic tools python without the venv site-packages.\n81|# We overwrite the inner launcher with a wrapper that finds the venv Python.\n82|COPY hermes-launcher.sh /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/bin/hermes\n83|RUN chmod 755 /opt/hermes-agent/.hermes/bin/hermes && \\\n84|    ln -sf /opt/hermes-agent/bin/hermes /usr/local/bin/hermes\n85|\n86|# ------------------------------------------------------------\n87|# 3. Connect your Hermes GUI client to http://host:8080\n11|# =============================================================================\n12|services:\n13|  hermes:\n14|    image: hermes-agent:latest\n15|    build:\n16|      context: .\n17|      # Optional: pin a specific Hermes commit\n18|      # args:\n19|      #   HERMES_COMMIT: abc123def\n20|    container_name: hermes\n21|    restart: unless-stopped\n22|    init: true\n23|\n24|    # ---- Port mapping ----\n25|    ports:\n26|      - \"${HERMES_PORT:-8080}:${HERMES_PORT:-8080}\"\n27|\n28|    # ---- Volumes ----\n29|    volumes:\n30|      # Persistent Hermes configuration (config.yaml + .env).\n31|      # Create it once manually or via `docker compose run --rm hermes-init`.\n32|      - ./hermes-config:/config:rw\n33|\n34|      # (Optional) Mount an existing Obsidian vault for full read/write access.\n35|      # Uncomment and point to your vault directory:\n36|      # - /absolute/path/to/your/vault:/vault:rw\n37|\n38|      # Read-only input data from host.\n39|      - ./input:/data/ro:ro\n40|\n41|      # Read-write working data from host.\n42|      - ./workspace:/data/rw:rw\n43|\n44|    # ---- Environment ----\n45|    environment:\n46|      - HERMES_PORT=${HERMES_PORT:-8080}\n47|      - HERMES_HOME=/config\n48|\n49|    # ---- Security hardening ----\n50|    read_only: false\n51|    security_opt:\n52|      - no-new-privileges:true\n53|    cap_drop:\n54|      - ALL\n55|    cap_add:\n56|      - CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE\n57|\n58|    # ---- Health check ----\n59|    # Hermes serve exposes no HTTP health endpoint; Ensure config.yaml exists (or create a minimal working one)\n7|#   2. Ensure the .env secrets file exists or warn\n8|#   3. Optionally detect a mounted Obsidian vault at /vault\n9|#   4. Start hermes in serve mode\n10|# =============================================================================\n11|set -euo pipefail\n12|\n13|HERMES_HOME=\"${HERMES_HOME:-/config}\"\n14|HERMES_PORT=\"${HERMES_PORT:-8080}\"\n15|CONFIG_FILE=\"${HERMES_HOME}/config.yaml\"\n16|ENV_FILE=\"${HERMES_HOME}/.env\"\n17|\n18|# -----------------------------------------------------------\n19|# Helper: create a minimal config.yaml\n20|# -----------------------------------------------------------\n21|create_minimal_config() {\n22|    echo \"==> No Hermes configuration found. Creating minimal config.yaml ...\"\n23|\n24|    cat > \"${CONFIG_FILE}\" <<- 'CONFEOF'\n25|# Minimal Hermes configuration — generated by docker-entrypoint.sh\n26|# Replace with your own config.yaml mounted at /config/config.yaml\n27|#\n28|# Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/configuration\n29|\n30|# --- Model provider (required for chat, optional for serve mode) ---\n31|# Set via `hermes config set` or editing this file.\n32|# Uncomment and set your preferred provider:\n33|#default_model: gpt-4o\n34|#default_provider: openai\n35|\n36|# --- Server mode (serve) ---\n37|# These defaults are overridden by CLI flags.\n38|server:\n39|  host: 0.0.0.0\n40|  port: ${HERMES_PORT}\n41|CONFEOF\n42|\n43|    sed -i \"s/\\${HERMES_PORT}/${HERMES_PORT}/g\" \"${CONFIG_FILE}\"\n44|    echo \"==> Created ${CONFIG_FILE}\"\n45|}\n46|\n47|# -----------------------------------------------------------\n48|# Helper: ensure .env exists or warn\n49|# -----------------------------------------------------------\n50|check_env_file() {\n51|    if [ ! -f \"${ENV_FILE}\" ]; then\n52|        cat > \"${ENV_FILE}\" <<- 'ENVEOF'\n53|# Hermes secrets — mount your own .env to /config/.env\n54|# API keys for LLM providers. At least one provider must be configured.\n55|# Examples:\n56|# OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...\n57|# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...\n58|# OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...\n59|ENVEOF\n60|        echo \"==> WARNING: ${ENV_FILE} is a stub. Add your API keys before starting Hermes.\"\n61|    fi\n62|}\n63|\n64|# -----------------------------------------------------------\n65|# Helper: detect and report an optional Obsidian vault mount\n66|# -----------------------------------------------------------\n67|check_vault_mount() {\n68|    if [ ! -d /vault ]; then\n69|        return\n70|    fi\n71|\n72|    if [ -z \"$(ls -A /vault 2>/dev/null)\" ]; then\n73|        echo \"==> /vault is present but empty — no Obsidian vault mounted.\"\n74|        return\n75|    fi\n76|\n77|    if [ -d /vault/.obsidian ]; then\n78|        echo \"==> Obsidian vault detected at /vault (full read/write access)\"\n79|    else\n80|        echo \"==> Directory mounted at /vault (no .obsidian marker found — still usable as a writable data dir)\"\n81|    fi\n82|}\n83|\n84|# -----------------------------------------------------------\n85|# Main\n86|# -----------------------------------------------------------\n87|cd /data/rw\n88|\n89|case \"${1:-serve}\" in\n90|    serve|server)\n91|        if [ ! -f \"${CONFIG_FILE}\" ]; then\n92|            create_minimal_config\n93|        else\n94|            echo \"==> Using existing config: ${CONFIG_FILE}\"\n95|        fi\n96|\n97|        check_env_file\n98|        check_vault_mount\n99|\n100|        if [ -d /data/rw ] && [ \"$(stat -c '%u' /data/rw)\" != \"$(id -u)\" ]; then\n101|            echo \"==> Adjusting /data/rw ownership to user $(id -un) ...\"\n102|            chown \"$(id -u):$(id -g)\" /data/rw 2>/dev/null || true\n103|        fi\n104|\n105|        echo \"==> Starting Hermes server on 0.0.0.0:${HERMES_PORT} ...\"\n106|        exec hermes serve \\\n107|            --host 0.0.0.0 \\\n108|            --port \"${HERMES_PORT}\" \\\n109|            --skip-build\n110|        ;;\n111|\n112|    init|setup)\n113|        echo \"==> Interactive Hermes setup mode.\"\n114|        echo \"==> Configure your provider, model, and credentials.\"\n115|        echo \"==> Type 'exit' or Ctrl-D when done.\"\n116|        echo \"\"\n117|        exec hermes setup\n118|        ;;\n119|\n120|    config)\n121|        shift\n122|        exec hermes config \"$@\"\n123|        ;;\n124|\n125|    shell|bash)\n126|        exec /bin/bash \"$@\"\n127|        ;;\n128|\n129|    *)\n130|        exec hermes \"$@\"\n131|        ;;\n132|esac", "total_lines": 132, "file_size": 4181, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

Danach gecached.\n\n## Einrichtung\n\n```bash\n# Config kopieren\ncp examples/config.openai.yaml hermes-config/config.yaml\n\n# API-Key setzen\necho \"OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-...\" > hermes-config/.env\n\n# Passwort-Hash generieren und in config.yaml eintragen\n./generate-password-hash.sh mein-passwort\n\n# Starten\ndocker compose up -d\n\n# Verbinden: http://<host>:8080 (User: admin, Passwort: selbst gesetzt)\n```\n\n## Auth (wichtig)\n\nSeit Juni 2026 verweigert Hermes den Bind auf `0.0.0.0` ohne Auth.\nAlle Beispiel-Configs haben einen `dashboard.basic_auth`-Block.\nDemo-Passwort: `admin/demo`. Eigenes generieren mit `generate-password-hash.sh`.\n\nAlternativen: SSH-Tunnel oder WireGuard auf `127.0.0.1`.\n\n## Autostart (systemd --user)\n\n```bash\ncp hermes-docker.service ~/.config/systemd/user/\n# In ~/.config/systemd/user/hermes-docker.service Pfad anpassen:\n#   WorkingDirectory=/daten/home/rb/_Syncthing/Ralf-Temporaer/_Arbeit/hermes-projekte/hermes-inside-docker\nsystemctl --user daemon-reload\nsystemctl --user enable hermes-docker\nsystemctl --user start hermes-docker\n```\n\nStartet Container bei Login, stoppt bei Logout.
